papers.2006ApJ...643.1011P: Paumard T. et al. 2006, ApJ 643, 1011 -- The two young star disks in the central parsec of the Galaxy (VizieR J/ApJ/643/1011)

caveats: Habibi 2017 final parameters are quoted from arXiv:1708.06353v1 (the only version); the published ApJ table could not be opened (ADS returned a human-verification page), so table numbering is the arXiv one (Table 2, which the body text calls Table 3).
Habibi 2017 gives the same 'B0-B3' type for all eight stars it fits (S1, S2, S4, S6, S7, S8, S9, S12); it is a group-level range, not individual subtypes.
Teff and mass uncertainties are asymmetric (err_plus/err_minus), from the BONNSAI posteriors. Masses are spectroscopic-evolutionary, not dynamical.

All RVs except S6 are the latest SINFONI value in Gillessen 2017 Table 5 (epochs 2016.284 / 2016.519), the LSR line-of-sight velocities used in that orbit fit. Table 5 has no RV for S6, S22, S23, S29; the S6 value is from Eisenhauer 2005 (2004.632).

S-star names changed between Eisenhauer 2005 and Gillessen 2009 for some objects (the Eisenhauer 2005 'S17' is an early-type double source at about -2000 km/s, unlike the late-type Gillessen S17), so Eisenhauer 2005 values were used only for S6, whose identity is pinned by Paumard 2006 and von Fellenberg 2022 cross-IDs.

Spectral type for S18, S19, S22, S23, S29 is only the Gillessen 2017 early-type flag. SIMBAD 'K-M' for [EG97] S19 (Do et al. 2009) conflicts with that flag and with von Fellenberg 2022 listing S19 as a young star.

No published per-star Teff or mass was found for S13, S14, S17, S18, S19, S21, S22, S23, S24, S29, S31. Habibi 2019 gives only group Teff ranges (4100-4600 K for the K0-K3.5 III giants) and a 0.5-2 Msun initial-mass range for late-type S-stars; not entered.

SIMBAD main IDs are the [EG97] designations; all 18 resolve. [EG97] S22 and S23 have no coordinates in SIMBAD. That SIMBAD [EG97] Sn is the same object as the Gillessen 2017 Sn was not checked by position.
GRAVITY 2018/2020 S2 papers were not opened (arXiv API was rate-limited during this run).
